teaching: Because the fork already exists and is not theirs, they must obtain access before pushing — via the /do:access comment command or the 'Request access' button on the Drupal.org fork management page — then use the existing fork. From there: branch, commit (Conventional Commits), push to the fork, and open the MR via the REST API (not glab mr create) with Closes #<id> to wire it to the issue.
prompt: I'm a first-time contributor to a Drupal module on git.drupalcode.org. There's an open work item I want to fix, but an issue fork already exists — someone else created it. Walk me through how to actually start working on it and get my change in.
response:
Good situation to clarify, because "a fork already exists" changes two steps versus the from-scratch path. Here's the walkthrough tailored to it.

## 0. Confirm your tooling (read-only is fine to start)

```bash
glab auth status --hostname git.drupalcode.org
```

If that fails, you need `glab` installed and authenticated before anything else. A read-only (Tier 1) token is enough for steps 1–2; you'll need a **write** token (Tier 2: add `api` or `write_repository`) for steps 3 onward.

## 1. Read the work item — and check for an existing MR

The repo name is the path segment right after `project/` in the URL.

```bash
glab issue view <id>  --repo "git.drupalcode.org/project/<repo>"
glab mr list          --repo "git.drupalcode.org/project/<repo>"
```

**This matters in your case.** Whoever created the fork may have already opened an MR from it. If an MR exists, you don't create a new one — you push your commits to its existing branch, and your work shows up on that same MR. Note the branch name (it'll look like `<issue-id>-some-description`).

## 2. Get access to the existing fork

The fork exists, so you skip `/do:fork`. As a first-timer you almost certainly **don't** have push access to someone else's fork yet. Check, then request:

```bash
# Can I see/push to it? (404 = fork doesn't exist; 403 on push = need access)
glab api --hostname git.drupalcode.org "/projects/issue%2F<repo>-<id>/members/all"
```

If you lack access, post a comment on the work item containing:

```
/do:access
```

That grants **your** user push access to the existing fork. (It's a Drupal.org custom command, not a normal GitLab one — all contributors can use it.)

## 3. Set up remotes

Two remotes: upstream (`origin`) and the issue fork. Mind the host — **SSH uses `git.drupal.org`** (the `drupalcode` CDN has no SSH listener and will hang on port 22):

```bash
# upstream, if not already cloned
git clone git@git.drupal.org:project/<repo>.git
# add the issue fork
git remote add fork git@git.drupal.org:issue/<repo>-<id>.git
git fetch fork
```

(If SSH is unavailable, use the HTTPS credential-helper pattern from the skill — never put the token in the URL.)

## 4. Branch from the right place

- **If an MR/branch already exists** (step 1): check out that branch so your commits land on the same MR — `git checkout -b <issue-id>-desc fork/<issue-id>-desc`.
- **If the fork exists but has no working branch yet:** create one named `<issue-id>-short-description` off the current target branch (often `1.0.x`, not `main` — confirm).

## 5. Commit in Conventional Commits format

```
fix: #<issue-id> Short summary of the change

Optional body explaining the why.

By: your-drupalorg-username
```

`By:` uses your **Drupal.org username**, not your GitLab display name or email.

## 6. Push to the fork (never to origin)

```bash
git push fork <branch-name>
```

CI fires on push, so this also kicks off the pipeline.

## 7. Open the MR — only if one doesn't already exist

If step 1 found no MR, create the cross-project one (`glab mr create` can't do fork→upstream, so use the REST API). First get the upstream numeric ID:

```bash
glab api --hostname git.drupalcode.org "/projects/project%2F<repo>"
```

Then create it from the fork to upstream, with `Closes #<id>` in the body and — **required** — the AI disclosure line if you used AI:

```
AI-Generated: Yes (Used [tool] to [how].)
```

The full API command with the body inline is in the skill's `merge-requests.md`. Set the title in `{type}: #{id} Summary` form, because GitLab squash-merges use the **MR title** as the commit message.

## 8. Signal it's ready, and claim credit

- Toggle the MR from **Draft → Ready** when it's ready for review (maps to Needs Review).
- Fill in the **contribution attribution** link DrupalBot posted on the work item (`new.drupal.org/contribution-record?source_link=…`) — on GitLab, credit is self-claimed, not granted in the commit.
- Merges happen via the **web UI** only — API/CLI merges are blocked here, so don't be surprised when `glab mr merge` won't work.

---

The two things that differ from the standard path because the fork already exists: **`/do:access` instead of `/do:fork`** (step 2), and **check for an existing MR before creating one** (steps 1 + 7).

If you paste the work item URL, I can run the read-only steps (view the item, check for an existing MR, check fork membership) and tell you exactly which branch to base off and whether you need `/do:access`.
